# Imgkeep

> Imgkeep is a free browser extension for Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge that saves web images as PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or PDF from the right-click menu. It converts each image on the user's computer (nothing is uploaded) and saves it to Downloads, a folder the user picks, or wherever they choose each time. It is open source under the MIT licence.

Key facts:

- Use: right-click an image, choose "Imgkeep: Save image as", then PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF (keeps animation), PDF or Original format. "Copy as PNG" puts the image on the clipboard.
- Converts the WebP and AVIF images many sites now serve into PNG or JPG files that every app opens. Animated WebP can be saved as an animated GIF.
- Privacy: images are converted on the device and never uploaded. No account. One anonymous daily count of which features were used and which saves failed is sent (never images, addresses or file names), and it can be turned off in Options.
- Find image here: on sites that cover their photos with another layer (like Instagram and Pinterest), a right-click can't reach the image. "Imgkeep: Find image here" looks at that page once, finds the photo under the click at its largest size, and opens it ready to save. Off until the user turns it on.
- Permissions: contextMenus, downloads, storage, offscreen. Two optional ones, activeTab and scripting, only if the user turns on Find image here. Imgkeep doesn't read the sites the user visits, except that one page when asked to find an image there, and it never changes a page. If a site blocks an image, Imgkeep asks for access to that one site, only after the user clicks to allow it.
- Price: free, no ads. A paid Imgkeep Pro with extra features is planned; current features stay free.
- Saves one image at a time (the one right-clicked), not every image on a page.
- Works in Chrome 116 and newer and in Microsoft Edge, in 9 languages.
- Free Image Converter at imgkeep.app/convert/: the same conversion code in a web page, for files already on a computer or phone. No uploads, no sign-up.

## Free Image Converter

- [Free Image Converter](https://imgkeep.app/convert/): converts WebP, AVIF, PNG, JPG, SVG and more to PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, PDF or ICO in the browser. No uploads, no sign-up: images never leave the device, and it works offline once loaded. Each result can be downloaded or copied as a PNG. Free, no ads, open source (same conversion code as the extension).
- [WebP to JPG](https://imgkeep.app/webp-to-jpg/): transparent areas get a background colour (white by default); quality 92 by default.
- [WebP to PNG](https://imgkeep.app/webp-to-png/): keeps transparency; animated WebP becomes one frame (choose GIF to keep motion).
- [AVIF to JPG](https://imgkeep.app/avif-to-jpg/): for apps and upload forms that can't open AVIF.
- [PNG to JPG](https://imgkeep.app/png-to-jpg/): smaller files for photos; choose quality and background colour.
- [PNG to ICO](https://imgkeep.app/png-to-ico/): one .ico with 16, 32 and 48 px icons, plus 256 px for large images.

- [Microsoft Edge Add-ons](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/kokbmagcbobpjclpidebikeklmpafhhd)

## Guides

- [Why Chrome saves images as WebP](https://imgkeep.app/chrome-saves-images-as-webp/): Chrome saves the file the site sent; many sites send WebP. No setting changes it; convert as you save or afterwards.
- [How to save WebP as JPG or PNG](https://imgkeep.app/save-webp-as-jpg-png/): with an extension in one step, or with Paint, Preview or copy and paste. Which format to pick.
- [How to save AVIF as JPG or PNG](https://imgkeep.app/save-avif-as-jpg-png/): what AVIF is, why apps refuse it, and how to convert it.
- [Chrome saves images as JFIF? How to get JPG](https://imgkeep.app/chrome-saves-images-as-jfif/): a .jfif file is a JPEG with a different ending, set by a Windows registry setting; rename it, fix the setting, or save as JPG.
- [How to save an animated WebP as a GIF](https://imgkeep.app/save-animated-webp-as-gif/): keep an animation moving (JPG and PNG keep one frame); what GIF keeps and loses; with an extension or GIMP.
- [How to save an image as a PDF in Chrome](https://imgkeep.app/save-image-as-pdf/): Chrome's print to PDF, Photos or Preview, or a one-page PDF the size of the image from the right-click menu.
- [A safe alternative to Save image as Type](https://imgkeep.app/save-image-as-type-alternative/): why Google removed it in March 2026, and a checklist for judging any image extension.
- [When right-click won't save an image](https://imgkeep.app/save-image-right-click-not-working/): why some sites cover their photos so the right-click can't reach them, the workarounds (developer tools, a screenshot), and Imgkeep's opt-in Find image here.
- [How to get an image from the web into Canva, Figma or Google Slides](https://imgkeep.app/web-image-into-canva-figma-google-slides/): copy it as a PNG and paste it, or save WebP or AVIF as PNG or JPG when a tool says the file type isn't supported; which formats each tool's help lists.
